item.description:

item.title: Civic Meetup #563: Canadian Council Records: Nothing but PDFs, and Toronto - by Civic Tech Toronto — Tue Oct 6, 7:00 PM — Hybrid
item.description:
More info: https://guild.host/events/civic-meetup-563-canadian-9q3r8p
Hosted by Civic Tech Toronto (https://civictech.ca/)
Most Canadian municipalities publish their council record as PDFs, sometimes scanned. A handful of SaaS vendors cover 500 cities between them; the rest are one-off formats, and then there's Toronto, whose minutes are a breath of fresh air. The speaker will show what it took to build a searchable record across both.

item.title: Soumendra Roy (Flatiron Institute, CCA) — Wed Oct 7, 11:00 AM — IdeaLab
item.description:
Title: Identity Crisis: Untangling Mass-Ordering Artifacts from Compact-Object Pairing in Gravitational-Wave Populations
Abstract: What can the observed masses of merging black holes tell us about how they form and pair? Answering this question requires accounting for a symmetry of the gravitational waveform: interchanging the two components leaves the waveform unchanged. We therefore label the heavier black hole the primary and the lighter one the secondary. This mass ordering can create fake structures in the population distribution of binary black hole mergers and complicate its astrophysical interpretation. Hence it is important to untangle mass-ordering effects from the physics of black hole pairing. In this talk, I will use increasingly general pairing cases to show which features mass ordering can and cannot mimic. item.title: Creating Custom Code Execution Engine Sandboxes For Your Loops And Harnesses — Tue Oct 13, 2:00 PM
item.description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto The last session showed how agent swarms can run safely on disposable, hardware-isolated compute.
This second session covers building the custom sandboxes that those agents need.
See how to package your own runtimes, dependencies, and tools as a custom container, expose it through Azure Container Apps Sandboxes, and operate it as a fast, isolated execution service.
Watch a custom engine move from container image to a managed session pool that agents can invoke on demand.
You'll learn • When to choose a custom sandbox • How to package specialized runtimes, libraries, binaries, and tools • Configuring prewarmed capacity, lifecycle policies, health probes, and automatic cleanup • Securing execution with isolation, network controls, managed identity, and tenant-aware session identifiers • Monitoring engine health, capacity, lifecycle events, and application output with Azure Monitor

item.description:
Menopause influences 70% of age-related diseases, yet less than 1% of preclinical aging studies worldwide consider menopause in their research. That’s why Sinai Health Foundation is inviting you to be bold, get cold and make a difference for women’s health by joining the Cold Plunge Challenge on Sunday, October 18th. You can plunge on your own at home, at your local spa or gym, or join us at Woodbine Beach for a community plunge in Lake Ontario. Registration for the in-person event is $15/person. Fundraising is encouraged to support research that aims to improve care and health outcomes for women, now and for the future. Help us transform care for women at every stage of life. Register today.

item.title: The Historic Eastern Beaches! (NEW FOR 2026) — Sun Oct 18, 2:00 PM
item.description:
Toronto History Walks \*\***The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email** [torontohistorywalks@gmail.com](http://torontohistorywalks@gmail.com%2A%2A/) **for more information or for signing up!\*\*** \*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket price when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:** [torontohistorywalks@gmail.com](http://torontohistorywalks@gmail.com%2A%2A/)
**This tour is a revised route for 2026.**
The area was first settled in 1794 by the Ashbridge family, whose name is remembered by the nearby bay and park. Their homestead on Queen Street East was well to the west of the area currently identified as the Beaches. A later generation of the Ashbridge family rebuilt the family home in 1854 and can be seen on Queen Street East opposite the TTC barns near Kingston Road.
